references.text: Joshua allocated land to the sons of Joseph and mentioned iron chariots as a hindrance to driving out the Canaanites in the valley plains.
The enemies had iron chariots, but the Lord gave Israel victory over them, showing that iron chariots were not an insurmountable obstacle when God intervened.
Sisera had 900 iron chariots, demonstrating the military superiority the Canaanites held in the valley plains.
Despite Sisera's 900 iron chariots, the Lord gave Israel victory, contrasting with Judah's inability to drive out the inhabitants of the valley.
When the Lord is not with His people, they suffer defeat at the hands of their enemies.
God promised to be with Israel in war, even against enemies with horses and chariots.
The Philistines gathered a large army with chariots against Israel, illustrating the threat posed by chariots in warfare.
